title: What If You Could UNDERSTAND Animals?
description:
Glint, 19, works nights at the city science museum. One night a power surge rips through the new Wild Voices sound dome, and when he wakes up on the floor he can decode what animals actually say: the pigeons, the prairie dogs, the bees, the whales, and finally Mr. Pickles. Then his best friend Kai vanishes in snowy Harrow Woods with forty minutes of daylight left, and the only signal that can find him is the one Kai can't escape: every crow in the city has learned his face, and hates it. The real science of animal communication (prairie dog alarm calls, the honeybee waggle dance, sperm whale codas and crows that remember faces) is the only map Glint has.

If you could understand animals, what would your pet say first? Tell me in the comments 👇

▶ More What Ifs: What If You Could Move 100x FASTER?

6:18 The Solution: Follow the crows
8:21 The Twist: Peanut face
9:08 Would you?

SOURCES
• Slobodchikoff et al., Animal Behaviour 42 (1991); Kiriazis & Slobodchikoff, Behavioural Processes (2006); Slobodchikoff, Paseka & Verdolin, Animal Cognition 12 (2009): prairie dog alarm calls encode predator type, size and colour; Slobodchikoff, Chasing Doctor Dolittle (2012)
• Nicastro, Journal of Comparative Psychology 118 (2004); Bradshaw, Cat Sense (2013): adult cats rarely meow at each other; meows are mainly for humans
• Humphrey et al., Scientific Reports 10: 16503 (2020): the cat slow blink as a friendly signal
• RSPB, "What to do if you find a baby bird": fledglings on the ground are usually watched by their parents
• Marzluff et al., Animal Behaviour 79 (2010); Cornell, Marzluff & Pecoraro, Proc. R. Soc. B 279 (2012): crows remember threatening faces for years and learn them from other crows
• Marzluff & Angell, Gifts of the Crow (2012): mobbing behaviour
• Karl von Frisch, Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine (1973); Seeley, Honeybee Democracy (2010): the waggle dance
• Rendell & Whitehead, Proc. R. Soc. B (2003); Hersh et al., PNAS (2022); Sharma et al., Nature Communications 15: 3617 (2024, Project CETI): sperm whale codas and clan dialects
• Story is fiction: Glint's power and every translated word are made up; the science rules are real.
